answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is exactly the memory I trust least: its readout is a four-week window in the standard SMB segment, which is long enough to see acquisition and booked revenue and too short to see discount-cohort retention, margin erosion, or renewal-time churn. A discount war against a competitor whose whole strategy is price also tends to buy the least durable accounts, which cuts directly against 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue.' So I spend one verification pull there — not because I expect to run it, but because if the archived record shows the lift was net of retention over a longer horizon, that materially changes the option, and if it shows the usual four-week proxy readout, I can retire it with confidence rather than vague suspicion.

My second pull is memory_86, because it underwrites the action I actually intend. memory_31 and memory_86 both point at onboarding but measure different things — memory_31 reports first-week activation from cutting signup fields, memory_86 reports completion rate and time-to-value from shortening onboarding. Completion rate is a proxy that can be gamed by removing steps that were doing real qualification work; if the original record shows shortening was achieved by dropping fit/qualification data, then 'simplify' could quietly degrade lead quality and reappear later as worse qualified revenue. I want the source before I commit, not after.

Intended action is simplify_onboarding. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and activation plausibly sits downstream of onboarding, so this is the closest thing to a root cause rather than a symptom; memory_91's activation messaging would likely be treating the downstream symptom. It is also the one direction where two independent inherited records (memory_31, memory_86) converge.

Caveats I am carrying forward rather than discarding: every supporting memory here is denominated in proxy metrics (completion, week-one engagement, first-week activation), none in retained qualified revenue; all are 24-52 days old and predate both the competitor's launch and the current declines, so the population may have shifted; and the inherited records are compressed summaries whose original guardrails I cannot see without pulling them. I am therefore running this as a standard experiment with a holdout and explicit downstream guardrails — lead-quality/fit mix, 30- and 60-day retention, and qualified pipeline per new account — not just completion rate, and not a broad rollout. If verification shows memory_86's lift came from stripping qualification, I will fall back to activation_messaging at the same guarded scale.
